title: Disposal of PPE
description: Calculate carrying amount and gains or losses when long-lived assets are sold or retired.
html:
What happens when PPE is sold?

Before calculating a gain or loss, the company needs to know the asset's carrying amount at the date of disposal.

Carrying Amount = Cost − Accumulated Depreciation

Then compare carrying amount with proceeds

Gain or Loss = Selling Price − Carrying Amount
  • If selling price is greater than carrying amount → Gain
  • If selling price is less than carrying amount → Loss
  • If selling price equals carrying amount → No gain or loss

Example 1 — Gain

Equipment originally cost $60,000. Accumulated depreciation is $42,000.

Carrying Amount = $60,000 − $42,000 = $18,000

The company sells the equipment for $22,000.

$22,000 − $18,000 = $4,000 Gain

Example 2 — Loss

Assume the same asset is sold for $15,000.

$15,000 − $18,000 = ($3,000) Loss

Important habit

Always calculate carrying amount first. Then compare it with the proceeds.

quiz.prompt: Equipment cost $90,000 and has accumulated depreciation of $65,000. It is sold for $30,000. What is the gain or loss?
quiz.explanation: Carrying amount is $90,000 − $65,000 = $25,000. Selling price of $30,000 exceeds carrying amount by $5,000, so there is a $5,000 gain.
